hero.title: NiceChunk contracts, live game configuration, and PDA transparency.
hero.subtitle: This page separates the game client's current runtime configuration from contracts that exist in code but are not referenced by that client configuration. A config omission is not an on-chain disable switch. Players can inspect source code, PDA structures, and public devnet accounts from one page.
hero.networkNote: The current game runtime points to Solana devnet through mainnet.json. Mainnet finality and live civilization governance are not claimed here.

directory.title: Current NiceChunk programs and runtime status.
directory.body: The table lists repository contracts, their program IDs, and whether the current game client references them. Client configuration does not by itself prove on-chain deployment or callability.

flow.title: How the current gameplay path touches the chain.

steps.title: Read Genesis Config
steps.body: The client derives GlobalConfig from the core program and reads world seed, chunk size, build limits, NCK mint, and published config hashes.
steps.writes: No user write; derives GlobalConfig PDA
steps.audit: GlobalConfig magic, world seed, hash fields, and runtime program IDs

steps.title: Create Player Profile
steps.body: The player program stores wallet-owned profile data, default attributes, position, equipment slots, and backpack style.
steps.audit: Owner wallet, profile name, position, equipped backpack, and update slot

steps.title: Open Mining Session
steps.body: A player can create an expiry-bearing session authority so repeated mining actions do not require wallet confirmation every block. The caller chooses the expiry, and the program sets no maximum duration or revoke path.
steps.writes: PlayerSession PDA with authority, action mask, expiry, and stored counters
steps.audit: Action mask and expiry are enforced; maxActions and actionCount are stored but not consumed

steps.title: Record Broken Blocks
steps.body: The chunk program verifies the generated single block, then writes a compact 3-byte broken-block record into the chunk-broken PDA.
steps.writes: ChunkBrokenState record under the Chunk program
steps.audit: Packed broken-block records, minY, count/capacity, and block proof assumptions

steps.title: Append Resources
steps.body: The backpack program is prepared to append mined resource records after session validation. It is the inventory-side bridge for the mining loop.
steps.writes: Backpack slot append or mutation through authorized program signer
steps.audit: Backpack owner, itemCount, slot payload, durability, material/item identity

steps.title: Smelt Resources Into Items
steps.body: The Smelting program validates a treasury-governed RecipeTable, matches selected Backpack inputs and fuels, removes them, and appends table-backed Material outputs through the smelting-authority PDA. Execution revalidates the table PDA, fixed authority, canonical GlobalConfig, and output provenance.
steps.writes: RecipeTable read plus Backpack remove/append through smelting authority
steps.audit: Selected table ID and authority provenance, recipe IDs, heat tiers, input/output volumes, disabled recipes, and output slot evidence

steps.title: List Backpack Items
steps.body: The marketplace reads the selected 80-byte slot from the seller Backpack PDA, removes that slot, and escrows the full slot snapshot inside the Listing PDA.
steps.audit: Seller, buyer, currency, price, escrow state, and original slot snapshot

steps.title: Settle Market Orders
steps.body: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.
steps.writes: Listing settlement and buyer Backpack delivery
steps.audit: Treasury fee routing, payment mint/native flag, settled slot, and final listing state

programs.name: NiceChunk Genesis Core
programs.role: One-time world configuration and NCK mint validation under the current program logic.
programs.summary: Under the current Core logic, initialize_global_config writes the GlobalConfig PDA once from compiled genesis parameters. The current dispatcher has no config-update or admin branch, but source code alone does not prove that the deployed program upgrade authority is closed.
instructions: Only the exact one-byte payload [0] is accepted; every other discriminator is invalid.
Validates SPL Token mint layout, decimals, initialized flag, genesis supply, disabled mint authority, and disabled freeze authority.
Creates or allocates the GlobalConfig PDA safely even if the PDA was pre-funded with dust lamports.
storage: World ID and 32-byte world seed.
Terrain, resource rule, and client world config hashes.
NCK mint, decimals, genesis supply, and development wallet.
Chunk size, section height, build limits, max terrain height, sea level, cooldowns, and guardian settings.
notes: The current program exposes no config update or admin instruction, but the source does not prove that the deployed program upgrade authority has been closed.
Future crafting, inventory, chunk state, world knowledge, and reputation systems belong in separate programs or future modules after PDA specs are finalized.
Devnet and testnet must use their own NCK mint; the mainnet mint should not be reused on development clusters.

programs.name: NiceChunk Player
programs.role: Wallet-owned player profile, position, equipment slots, backpack style, and mining session authority.
programs.summary: The Player program creates a wallet-bound profile and an expiry-bearing session authority. Consumers enforce signer binding, action mask, and expiry, but the caller may choose an arbitrarily distant expiry and there is no revoke/close path or enforced action counter.
instructions: All other player tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: Owner wallet, GlobalConfig address, world ID, bump, and timestamps.
Base attributes: health, energy, stamina, mining power, build power, and defense.
Current position and nine equipment slots.
Session authority, allowed action bitmask, expiration time, and stored maxActions/actionCount fields.
notes: The profile is public state. It stores the equipped backpack public key, while private backpack contents are loaded separately when the player opens inventory flows.
The current session model is used to reduce repeated wallet prompts during mining.

Current consumers enforce signer binding, expiration, and allowed action flags. They do not check or increment maxActions/actionCount, impose a maximum session duration, or provide revoke/close; refreshing an existing session requires both the owner and existing session authority to sign.

programs.name: NiceChunk Skills
programs.kind: Authoritative XP, level, and progression-rule layer
programs.role: Stores ten authoritative XP totals and levels per owner, consumes validated source counters, and applies mining-only Swiftness and Burden awards.
programs.summary: The Skills program is the single level authority. PlayerSkills stores XP, cached levels, source cursors, mining travel state, and burden work. Treasury-governed SkillRuleTable thresholds and source rules determine every accepted delta; mining-only awards also require a matching Chunk instruction in the same transaction.
instructions: All other skill tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: PlayerSkills stores ten u64 XP totals, ten cached levels, 32 source cursors, the applied rule revision, and creation/update slots.
Mining state stores the last proven coordinate, qualifying travel count, accumulated burden work, and the last consumed Backpack mining sequence.
SkillRuleTable stores ten cumulative thresholds for each of ten skills, up to 30 generic source rules, one travel rule, and one burden rule.
Source rules bind a program owner, account magic, PDA seed layout, metric offset, bounded sync delta, divisor, and per-skill XP rates.
notes: The browser does not merge local XP with chain XP; PlayerSkills is the authoritative ledger.
Generic source synchronization validates account owner, PDA, magic, owner/global-config fields, monotonic counters, and a bounded delta.
Swiftness distance and Burden mass awards require an Instructions sysvar proof of a matching Chunk mining instruction in the same transaction.
Changing thresholds increments the rule revision; the next sync recomputes cached levels from the same cumulative table.

programs.name: NiceChunk Chunk
programs.role: Verifies generated single blocks and records compact broken-block state per chunk.
programs.accountSize: ChunkBrokenState: 16-byte header + 3 bytes per capacity record; rule and foundation indexes use separate layouts
programs.summary: The chunk program uses the current optimized mining path. For mining, the player submits one world block coordinate. The program derives the chunk, verifies the generated block, rejects air/water/bedrock or already-mined positions, and appends a compressed broken-block record.
storage: ChunkBrokenState stores a 16-byte header and 3-byte mined-block records; the dispatcher exposes only the final mining instruction surface.
ResourceDropTable, SurfaceDecorationTable, and FoundationChunk accounts keep rule and occupied-foundation evidence in separate PDA families.
A record packs local x, local z, and y offset. Capacity starts at 64, grows by 64, and caps at 2,048 records.
GlobalConfig world seed, chunk size, build height, max terrain height, and sea level are used for generated block verification.
notes: This is the current mining write path used by the browser client.
Backpack resource settlement is intentionally separate so mining state and inventory state can evolve independently.

pdaAccounts.name: ChunkBrokenState
pdaAccounts.purpose: Sparse record of generated blocks broken by players.
fields: grows by capacity instead of storing full terrain

programs.name: NiceChunk Unified Game Router
programs.role: Consumes a one-byte namespace envelope and forwards the remaining payload to Backpack, Chunk, Smelting, or Market logic compiled into one executable.
programs.sdk: No standalone SDK; callers prepend a namespace byte to the child-module payload.
programs.summary: The unified Game program dispatches namespace 1 to Backpack, 2 to Chunk, 3 to Smelting, and 4 to Market, passing the same incoming program ID into the selected child processor. public/mainnet.json currently aliases Backpack, Market, and Smelting to this executable while Chunk remains separately routed. The selected cluster feature must propagate to every child crate so mint and cluster constants cannot silently remain on Devnet in a testnet or mainnet build.
instructions: An empty payload or any other namespace returns InvalidInstruction (custom error 6600).
pdaSeeds: No router-owned seed domain; unified child PDAs derive under the incoming Game program ID.
storage: The router owns no separate state layout and writes only through the selected child module.
The first byte is removed before the child module reads its own instruction discriminator.
notes: Wire format is [namespace, childTag, childPayload...], not the standalone child payload by itself.
Equal runtime IDs for logical labels are routing aliases, not proof of independent deployments.
Devnet, testnet, and mainnet features forward to every routed child dependency; conflicting or missing cluster selection is rejected at compile time.

programs.name: NiceChunk Building
programs.kind: Immutable chunk-aligned land and NCM3 building manifests
programs.role: Reserves treasury-issued land contracts, registers BuildSite v3 chunks, and finalizes NCM3 buildings for direct on-chain discovery.
programs.accountSize: BuildSite: 160 bytes; BuildingManifest: 160 bytes; BuildingShard: 64 + payload bytes
programs.summary: The Building program reserves one treasury-issued land contract per complete 16x16 chunk, registers immutable BuildSite v3 land, consumes the reservation atomically on the final chunk, and reverses registered indexes before returning contracts when an incomplete site is canceled.
instructions: 0 create_build_site and reserve the required land contracts
1 register_build_site_chunks and consume the reservation after the final chunk
6 cancel_build_site_indexing, remove registered chunks in reverse order, and release contracts
All other building tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: BuildSite stores the owner, global config, foundation ID, chunk-aligned footprint, blank-contract type and count, revision state, and indexing counters.
BuildingManifest stores one finalized NCM3 building revision, dimensions, offsets, hash, shard bitmap, and activation state under the v3 building namespace.
BuildingShard stores one bounded payload segment under the v2 shard namespace, with payload bytes after its 64-byte header.
notes: One blank land contract covers one complete 16x16 chunk; a parcel consumes chunksX multiplied by chunksZ contracts and is capped at 4,096 contracts.
Active land cannot be resized or canceled. Incomplete indexing can be canceled only by removing registered FoundationChunk entries in reverse order before releasing the full reservation.
Nearby clients derive FoundationChunk v3 PDAs, validate each referenced BuildSite, and compare the complete BuildingManifest SHA-256 before reusing cached NCM3 bytes.

programs.name: NiceChunk Guardian Registry
programs.kind: Regional relay registration, liveness proofs, settlement, and endpoint discovery
programs.role: Registers 100x100-Chunk relay regions, records operator proofs, settles stale regions, and lets the region owner update its endpoint.
programs.summary: Guardian is a realtime relay registry. It does not index land, publish building summaries, validate BuildingManifest accounts, or participate in land-contract consumption.
instructions: 5 update_guardian_endpoint with the region owner signature
All other Guardian tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: GuardianRegistry stores GlobalConfig, NCK mint and treasury token identities, active and total registration counters, genesis state, region size, stake policy, and creation metadata.
GuardianRegion V1 stores owner, operator, GlobalConfig, endpoint, stake and proof lifecycle fields for one 100x100-Chunk region.
notes: Guardian realtime messages are availability hints, not authoritative land or building state.
Land and buildings are discovered from FoundationChunk, BuildSite, BuildingManifest, and BuildingShard PDAs without a Guardian dependency.
Endpoint mutation requires the stored region owner; proof submission requires the stored operator.

programs.name: NiceChunk Backpack
programs.kind: Inventory slot layer for blocks, resources, and items
programs.role: Creates player backpacks, maintains authoritative volume and mass, stores resource and item slots, and creates immutable forged-model accounts.
programs.accountSize: BackpackAccount v4: 8,048 bytes; MaterialPhysicsTable: 1,040 bytes; ForgedItem: 752 bytes
programs.summary: The Backpack program stores v4 fixed-size slots, enforces per-slot and total mass from MaterialPhysicsTable, records pre-mine mass and mining sequence for Burden XP, and creates immutable ForgedItem model PDAs. Marketplace, Smelting, Chunk, Player equipment, and Skills consume explicit PDA-gated paths.
instructions: All other backpack tags return InvalidInstruction.
9 retired construction-item issuance: always returns InvalidInstruction
pdaSeeds: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.
storage: Backpack v4 stores owner, capacity, item count, placement, timestamps, total mass, the pre-mine mass snapshot, action ID, and mining sequence.
Default capacity is 50 slots and maximum capacity is 99 slots; every slot is a fixed 80-byte record.
Each slot stores kind, category, flags, quantity, resource coordinate, item identity, volume, mass, durability, grade, level, quality, and metadata.
MaterialPhysicsTable maps block and item keys to density in kg/m³ and standard volume in mm³.
ForgedItem stores immutable canonical NCF1 bytes separately from the movable Backpack slot that references it.
notes: Backpack v4 requires an initialized mass state; old Backpack account layouts are intentionally unsupported on testnet.
Every material-bearing append validates or derives mass from the current MaterialPhysicsTable before updating totalMassGrams.
Tag 13 snapshots pre-mine mass and advances a monotonic mineSequence so Skills can award Burden XP once per proven mining action.
Marketplace and equipment move slot custody, while an immutable ForgedItem PDA remains the canonical model proof.
Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.
Backpack v4 compacts and discards historical construction-item slots; they cannot be issued, equipped, listed, or used to register land.

programs.name: NiceChunk Smelting
programs.kind: Recipe table and backpack item creation layer
programs.role: Stores smelting recipe tables, consumes selected backpack resources and fuels, and appends material or item outputs back into the backpack.
programs.summary: The smelting program separates fixed recipe governance from Backpack storage. A RecipeTable PDA stores up to 10 recipes, each with up to 8 input slots and 4 output slots. Only the compiled treasury may initialize or directly upsert a table; execution validates owner, stored ID, PDA, bump, fixed authority, canonical GlobalConfig, and table-backed Material outputs.
instructions: execute_smelting supports input indexes, fuel indexes, and a batch multiplier.
storage: RecipeTable stores table ID, authority, recipe count, timestamps, and fixed-size recipe records.
Each RecipeRecord stores recipe ID, enabled flag, minimum heat tier, input count, output count, up to 8 input BackpackSlot records, up to 4 output BackpackSlot records, and updated slot.
BackpackSlot records support block resources and item/material outputs.
Direct recipe upsert requires the compiled treasury signer. The Smelting instruction map exposes no recipe-authority transfer branch.
notes: Only the compiled treasury signer may initialize an unused table ID; a validated Civilization receipt can separately patch its exact target table.
Execution validates backpack ownership, recipe matching, input slots, fuel slots, and batch multiplier before consuming inventory.
The smelting-authority PDA gates Backpack writes, while execution separately validates the RecipeTable identity, fixed treasury authority, and table-backed Material output provenance.

pdaAccounts.name: RecipeTable
pdaAccounts.purpose: Authority-owned smelting recipe table used by the smelting program.
fields: each recipe stores heat tier, input slots, output slots and updatedSlot

pdaAccounts.name: SmeltingAuthority
pdaAccounts.purpose: Program signer used to append outputs only after the Smelting program validates RecipeTable identity and table-backed Material provenance.

programs.name: NiceChunk Marketplace
programs.kind: Escrow marketplace and treasury-issued land contracts
programs.role: Escrows transferable inventory listings and sells blank land contracts directly from the treasury without creating Listing PDAs.
programs.summary: The unified Game/Market program settles item listings and maintains MarketUser v1 membership. A treasury purchase transfers exactly 1 NCK per blank land contract and credits the buyer's available contract balance without creating a Listing PDA.
instructions: 4 buy_treasury_contract at exactly 1 NCK per blank land contract
Listing settlement supports NCK and SOL with a 1% market fee; treasury land-contract purchases do not create listings or charge that fee.
pdaSeeds: LandContractAuthority is derived by Building: ["land-contract-authority-v1", globalConfig]
storage: Listing stores seller, listing ID, currency, source type/index, price, the full 80-byte escrowed source slot, buyer, and settlement fields.
MarketUser v1 stores owner, active listing count, updated slot, available blank land contracts at bytes 52-55, and reserved contracts at bytes 56-59.
Blank land contracts are balances inside MarketUser, not Backpack items; they use no Backpack slot and no Listing account when purchased from the treasury.
notes: Each wallet may have at most 50 active listings.
Each treasury purchase may buy 1 to 4,096 blank land contracts at a fixed price of 1 NCK each.
Only the Building program's land-contract authority can reserve, consume, or release contract balances.
Historical construction-item records are discarded and cannot be transferred or used to register land.

pdaAccounts.purpose: Program signer for escrow restore, delivery, and settlement authority boundaries.
fields: Does not custody player wallets outside explicit instructions

pdaAccounts.name: MarketUser
pdaAccounts.purpose: Membership, active listing limit, and available/reserved blank land-contract balances.

programs.name: NiceChunk Civilization
programs.status: Implemented / not in current client config
programs.role: Publishes rulebooks, signatures, tallies, execution receipts, Civilization Value snapshots, and citizen power accounts.
programs.magic: NCKCVR01 / NCKCVS01 / NCKCVT01 / NCKCVE01 / NCKCVP01 / NCKCVC01
programs.accountSize: RuleBook: 320; Signature: 136; Tally: 128; Receipt: 128; PowerSnapshot: 128; CitizenPower: 144 bytes
programs.summary: The Civilization program exists in the repository and SDK, but it is not part of the current mainnet.json game runtime configuration yet. It records proposals, signatures, caller-supplied tallies, execution receipts, and authority-settled power. The current code has no enforced voting window and does not prove that every available signature was included in a tally.
instructions: All other civilization tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: RuleBook stores hashes, target program/PDA, threshold, risk level, total power, required power, and tally counters.
RuleSignature stores signer side and settled snapshot power.
PowerSnapshot stores authority-signed total active power, epoch fields, hash, and expiresAt; tally does not compare the stored epoch range with Clock.
CitizenPower stores a power amount bound to one snapshot. expiresAt is checked during settlement and signing, but tally does not re-check signature age, expiry, or epoch fields.
notes: The current game client does not submit Civilization instructions because mainnet.json omits its program ID; this client-side omission does not disable direct calls if the program is deployed.
Civilization Value cannot be self-reported; power snapshots and citizen power settlement require the configured authority signer.
Players can inspect the intended PDA structure here, but deployment and on-chain program authority must be verified separately before treating any records as live.

recipe-table.title: RecipeTable
recipe-table.body: Authority-owned smelting recipe table used by the smelting program.
recipe-table.visible: Authority, recipe count, update slot, heat tiers, input counts, output counts, and recipe IDs.
recipe-table.trust: Shows recipes in the selected table; execution additionally validates the PDA from stored table ID and bump plus the compiled treasury authority.

market-listing.title: MarketplaceListing
market-listing.body: Public marketplace listing state for a backpack slot.
market-listing.visible: Seller, listing ID, currency, source index, full source slot, price, buyer, and final state.
market-listing.trust: Market escrow and settlement can be audited without trusting a private order book.

forged-items.title: Forged item records
forged-items.body: A convenience scan that finds forged outputs inside live Backpack accounts.
forged-items.visible: Source account type, owner, backpack identity, forged sample slots, item code, and item ID.
forged-items.trust: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

civilization-rule-book.title: Civilization RuleBook
civilization-rule-book.visible: Author, hashes, target program/PDA, threshold, risk level, tally counters, and status.
civilization-rule-book.trust: Shows proposal targets and the author-selected threshold, which may be as low as 1 bps; it does not prove a voting window or complete tally.

civilization-rule-signature.title: Civilization signatures
civilization-rule-signature.body: One citizen signature record for a rule.
civilization-rule-signature.visible: Signer, side, snapshot hash, snapshot power, and signed time.
civilization-rule-signature.trust: Signature power comes from settled Civilization Value, not self-reported numbers.

civilization-rule-tally.title: Civilization tallies
civilization-rule-tally.visible: Agree, reject, abstain, challenge power, required power, and threshold result.
civilization-rule-tally.trust: Shows the threshold result for the signature accounts supplied by the finalizer; it does not prove every available signature was counted.

civilization-execution-receipt.title: Civilization execution receipts
civilization-execution-receipt.body: Account recording rule execution or acknowledgement.
civilization-execution-receipt.visible: RuleBook, executor, executed slot, and timestamp.
civilization-execution-receipt.trust: Binds a receipt to its RuleBook and stored threshold result; it does not prove that all signatures were counted or that a voting window elapsed.

civilization-power-snapshot.title: Civilization Value snapshots
civilization-power-snapshot.visible: Authority, snapshot hash, total active power, window, and expiry.
civilization-power-snapshot.trust: Shows authority-declared power, epoch fields, and expiry; the current tally path does not enforce the stored epoch window against Clock.

civilization-citizen-power.title: CitizenPower accounts
civilization-citizen-power.body: One citizen power amount bound to a snapshot; the epoch range is stored metadata rather than an enforced tally window.
civilization-citizen-power.visible: Citizen, snapshot, power, settled slot, and expiry.
civilization-citizen-power.trust: Shows settled signer power used at signature time; finalization does not re-check expiry or include every available signature automatically.

transparency.title: Players can audit the world from contract code to public PDA state.
transparency.body: NiceChunk treats public state as part of the game interface. Players should be able to inspect who exists, which backpacks and listings exist, what recipes are active, which regions serve realtime play, and which rules or accounts are still only planned.

cards.title: Players are public account records, not hidden rows in a private database.
cards.body: PlayerProfile and PlayerSession PDAs expose the wallet, position, equipped backpack pointer, session authority, enforced action mask and expiry, and stored counter fields that current consumers do not enforce.
points: Enforced session mask/expiry and non-enforced counter fields are distinguishable.

cards.title: Backpacks and market listings are readable storage objects.
cards.body: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.
points: Forged items surface through Backpack item slots.

cards.title: Terrain and mining state are tied to verifiable world config.
cards.body: GlobalConfig fixes the world seed and config hashes, while ChunkBrokenState and ResourceDropTable expose what has been mined and which extra-drop rules exist.
points: World seed and hashes are public.
Broken-block records are compact but readable.
Drop tables are bounded PDA data.

cards.title: Civilization records require separate deployment and state verification.
cards.body: The Civilization contract defines rulebooks, signatures, caller-supplied tallies, receipts, and Civilization Value accounts. Its ID is absent from the current client config, which does not itself disable a deployed program.
points: Client runtime config and on-chain availability are separate.
Rule targets must point to inspectable PDAs.

Read Backpack accounts to inspect owners, capacity, item counts, block resources, and item/material slots.
Read forged records from Backpack item slots without inventing a separate live forging program.
Read RecipeTable accounts to inspect active recipe tables, heat tiers, input counts, output counts, and update slots.
Read BuildSite, BuildingManifest, and BuildingShard accounts to inspect foundation footprints, upload progress, active revisions, and NCM3 payload metadata.
Read GuardianRegistry and 256-byte GuardianRegion V1 accounts to audit endpoint, owner/operator roles, stake, proofs, penalties, and settlement state.
Read MarketplaceListing accounts to inspect seller, buyer, price, currency, escrowed slot, state, and settlement slots.
Read RuleBook, signature, tally, receipt, power snapshot, and citizen power accounts to inspect the governance path.

runtime.title: What the game client is actually configured to use now.
runtime.body: This section reads the public mainnet.json runtime index and separates programs referenced by the current game client from contracts that exist in code. Omission from this file is not an on-chain disable switch.

config.label: Runtime index
config.title: The game still uses the public runtime config.
config.body: mainnet.json reports cluster {cluster} and app version {version}. It remains the high-frequency game config, not a website i18n bundle.

programs.label: Active programs
programs.title: Programs currently referenced by the game client.
programs.body: These are the client routing IDs currently supplied by mainnet.json. They select executables for this build; by themselves they do not prove deployed ELF identity, ProgramData upgrade authority, or independent deployments for logical module labels.

alias.label: Shared game program
alias.title: Some modules currently point to the same program ID.
alias.body: This reflects the current client configuration: backpack, smelting, and market map to one shared executable ID. Chunk has its own configured ID, and configuration alone does not prove deployment state.

civilization.label: Civilization
civilization.title: Civilization exists in code but is not referenced by the current game client.
civilization.bodyConfigured: The Civilization program is present in the runtime configuration.
civilization.bodyGated: The Civilization program is documented and decodable here, but it is not in the current mainnet.json runtime config. That omission alone neither proves it is undeployed nor prevents direct calls to a deployed program.

auditMatrix.title: What an external reviewer should verify for each contract surface.
auditMatrix.body: This matrix ties each program to the authority gate, PDA evidence, live proof, and current boundary that can be checked without trusting a private server.

rows.intent: Proves that world constants and program IDs are derived from a public configuration account.
rows.authority: The current Core dispatcher writes GlobalConfig once and exposes no update branch; deployed program upgrade authority must be verified separately.
rows.evidence: GlobalConfig PDA, config hash fields, NCK mint, world seed, chunk dimensions, Guardian parameters.
rows.live: Compare /mainnet.json with the GlobalConfig PDA in the RPC browser.
rows.boundary: Core does not mint items, mutate terrain, update inventory, or execute governance.

rows.intent: Shows which wallet owns a public player profile and which expiry-bearing session may submit masked actions; no maximum duration or revoke path is enforced.
rows.authority: Owner wallet initializes profile/session state; consumers enforce the session signer, action mask, and expiry, but not maxActions/actionCount.
rows.evidence: PlayerProfile, PlayerSession, PlayerAppearance, and equipment PDA records.
rows.live: Read player-profile and player-session groups, then match owner, session authority, and update slot.
rows.boundary: A cached browser wallet is not proof of control; the PDA owner and signatures are the trust boundary.

rows.intent: Makes every accepted XP delta, threshold, cached level, and anti-replay cursor publicly inspectable.
rows.authority: The stored rule-table authority manages thresholds and source rules; sync accepts only source accounts whose program, PDA, magic, owner, GlobalConfig, metric, and monotonic counter match the configured rule.
rows.evidence: PlayerSkills, SkillRuleTable, source cursors, rule revision, mining coordinate proof, Backpack mass snapshot, and mining sequence.
rows.live: Scan player-skills and skill-rule-table accounts, then compare their revision, source cursors, thresholds, and mining state with the source progress PDAs.
rows.boundary: Browser previews and local counters are not XP authority. Mining-only awards require a matching Chunk instruction in the same transaction.

rows.intent: Separates generated terrain proof from the sparse record of blocks that have actually been mined.
rows.authority: Chunk logic recomputes the target block from GlobalConfig and rejects invalid, protected, or already broken blocks.
rows.evidence: ChunkBrokenState packed records, ResourceDropTable, SurfaceDecorationTable, minY, count, and capacity.
rows.live: Scan ChunkBrokenState and ResourceDropTable accounts for the target world and chunk coordinates.
rows.boundary: The program stores sparse mutations, not the full terrain; inventory settlement is handled by Backpack.

rows.intent: Makes the one-byte namespace envelope and the address domain used by compiled child processors explicit.
rows.authority: Only namespaces 1-4 are accepted. The router removes that byte and passes the incoming Game program ID, accounts, and remaining child payload into Backpack, Chunk, Smelting, or Market logic.
rows.evidence: The router owns no account state; routed child PDA derivation and account ownership checks use the incoming Game program ID.
rows.live: Compare the current mainnet.json aliases (Backpack, Market, and Smelting to Game; Chunk standalone) with the exact built and deployed ELF.
rows.boundary: Configuration and source do not prove the deployed ProgramData or upgrade authority, and logical aliases are not independent deployments.

rows.intent: Shows whether a player-owned foundation and uploaded NCM3 building payload were validated before publication.
rows.authority: PlayerProfile and PlayerSession gate BuildSite writes, but current Building branches request BREAK_BLOCK rather than the defined PLACE_BLOCK action bit.
rows.evidence: Guardian is limited to realtime relay registration, liveness, settlement, and endpoint discovery; land and buildings are read directly from Chunk and Building PDAs.
rows.live: Inspect build-site, building-manifest, and building-shard accounts; compare footprint, revision, hash, dimensions, and shard bitmap.
rows.boundary: A manifest only becomes active after every shard is present and the payload hash and fit checks pass.

rows.intent: Lets a reviewer inspect which realtime relay regions exist, who owns each registration, which operator proves liveness, and which endpoint is advertised.
rows.authority: Any payer may initialize the deterministic Registry against its pinned treasury token. The Region owner signs registration and endpoint changes, the stored operator signs proofs, and settlement is permissionless.
rows.evidence: GuardianRegistry and GuardianRegion V1 records with owner, operator, endpoint, proof timestamps, proof count, remaining stake, penalties, and update slot.
rows.live: Scan guardian-registry and 256-byte guardian-region accounts, then compare PDA derivation, roles, endpoint, proof cadence, remaining stake, and settlement counters.
rows.boundary: There is no withdrawal, refund, owner setter, or operator-rotation instruction. Guardian is realtime service state and never gates land or building acceptance.

rows.intent: Keeps mined resources, item references, and custody transfers visible as fixed-size slot records.
rows.authority: Owner and program-PDA paths mutate slots, and Backpack tag 2 also accepts a BREAK_BLOCK session that may remove any selected slot index.
rows.evidence: Backpack PDA, itemCount, 80-byte slot payloads, source coordinates, material or item identity, durability.
rows.live: Scan backpack accounts and verify itemCount, slot type, material IDs, item hashes, and source coordinates.
rows.boundary: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

rows.intent: Shows which validated treasury-governed RecipeTable drove material conversion and which table PDA backs each Material output.
rows.authority: Only the compiled treasury may initialize or directly upsert a table; execution accepts only identity-valid tables with that stored authority and table-backed Material outputs.
rows.evidence: RecipeTable records, recipe IDs, heat tiers, input and output volumes, disabled recipe flags.
rows.live: Read recipe-table accounts and compare them with public/rules/smelting-rules.json and Backpack output slots.
rows.boundary: Execution checks program ownership, stored ID, PDA, bump, fixed treasury authority, and output provenance. Reviewers still identify the selected table ID because the program does not read the website configuration list.

rows.intent: Shows whether a listed asset is a concrete Backpack slot snapshot and how settlement returns or delivers it.
rows.authority: Seller signs the listing; market authority escrows, cancels, or delivers the exact slot snapshot.
rows.evidence: MarketplaceListing, seller, buyer, currency, price, escrowed slot bytes, settlement status.
rows.live: Scan market-listing accounts and compare original slot snapshot, buyer, fee routing, and final state.
rows.boundary: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

rows.intent: Makes rule proposals, signatures, power snapshots, caller-supplied tallies, and execution receipts auditable without treating them as complete or windowed approval.
rows.authority: A fixed power authority settles power; any payer may propose, finalize a caller-supplied signature subset, and execute after that subset's recorded threshold result passes.
rows.evidence: RuleBook, RuleSignature, RuleTally, ExecutionReceipt, PowerSnapshot, CitizenPower.
rows.live: Use the Civilization PDA groups to inspect records if the program is deployed. The current mainnet.json omission describes client wiring and does not block direct on-chain submission.
rows.boundary: Target adapters bind governable writes, but proposal threshold may be as low as 1 bps, no voting window is enforced, and a tally need not include every available signature.

logic.title: Understand the contracts as a connected trust graph.
logic.body: Each map shows the actor, program boundary, PDA evidence, and public verification surface. The goal is to explain what the contracts actually protect before a reader opens the code or RPC browser.

diagrams.body: The client can prepare instructions, but durable game state appears only after the wallet, session authority, and program checks agree on the same GlobalConfig and owner relationship.

nodes.label: Rule author
nodes.detail: Publishes a rulebook with target program, target PDA, payload hash, and required power.

nodes.label: Citizen signer
nodes.detail: Signs agree, reject, abstain, or challenge against the exact RuleBook and settled power snapshot.

nodes.detail: Binds execution of the stored threshold result to the target program; it does not establish that the tally was complete or windowed.

nodes.detail: One signer-side record that binds vote side and power to the exact rulebook.

nodes.detail: Aggregates only the signature accounts supplied by the finalizer and records whether that subset met the stored threshold.

nodes.label: PowerSnapshot
nodes.detail: Authority-settled total active power used to validate impossible signature sets.

nodes.detail: Per-citizen power whose expiry is checked when signing; tally can later count the stored signature without re-checking expiry or epoch fields.

seedEvidence.body: These graphs turn the Rust and SDK seed constants into a reviewer-facing evidence map, so drift in PDA names, signer boundaries, or runtime assumptions is easy to spot.

diagrams.body: The world layer derives generated terrain from GlobalConfig, then records only sparse public evidence for broken blocks, foundation occupancy, resource drops, decoration rules, and player progress.

nodes.label: GlobalConfig
nodes.detail: The one-time config account storing world seed, dimensions, mint data, and hashes under current Core program logic.

nodes.label: mainnet.json
nodes.detail: The browser runtime chooses cluster and program IDs from this public file before reading PDAs.

nodes.label: ChunkBrokenState
nodes.detail: Stores compact 3-byte records for mined blocks inside one chunk.

nodes.label: FoundationChunk
nodes.detail: Indexes which foundations occupy a chunk so build and mining checks share a public conflict witness.

nodes.detail: A global-config-scoped extra-drop rule table. The current seed is resource-drops-v2 and does not include a table ID.

nodes.label: PlayerProgress
nodes.detail: Tracks per-owner progress under the program that awards the action, scoped by GlobalConfig.

nodes.label: Owner wallet
nodes.detail: Funds and signs profile, backpack, market, equipment, and allowed action setup.

nodes.label: Session authority
nodes.detail: Submits action-mask-approved calls until a caller-chosen expiry; no maximum duration, revoke, or consumed counter is enforced.

nodes.detail: Lets the Player and Backpack programs move a custodied equipment slot without giving arbitrary write access.

Session does not replace owner custody
Historical construction-item identities are not part of the active marketplace or land flow

instructionSurface.title: Trace every accepted instruction tag to the gate that handles it.
instructionSurface.body: These maps mirror the current Rust process_instruction match arms, including retired and invalid tags, so SDK builders and reviewers can spot stale integration assumptions before they reach chain calls.

diagrams.title: One namespace byte selects a compiled child processor without changing the incoming program ID.
diagrams.body: Calls to nicechunk_game use [namespace, childTag, childPayload...]. The router removes only the namespace byte, then passes the original accounts and incoming Game program ID to the selected child logic. Unified child PDA checks therefore derive under the Game executable ID. In the current mainnet.json, Backpack, Market, and Smelting use that route while Chunk remains standalone.

nodes.label: Game instruction data
nodes.detail: The first byte is the namespace. The next byte is the selected child's own instruction tag, followed by that child's payload bytes.

nodes.label: Incoming Game program ID
nodes.detail: The router forwards the same program_id reference instead of substituting the standalone child crate ID.

nodes.label: Namespace 1
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Backpack logic.

nodes.label: Namespace 2
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Chunk logic when Game is the addressed executable.

nodes.label: Namespace 3
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Smelting logic.

nodes.label: Namespace 4
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Market logic.

nodes.label: Backpack processor
nodes.detail: Reads the child tag after namespace 1 has been removed.

nodes.label: Chunk processor
nodes.detail: Can run inside Game through namespace 2, although the current client config addresses the standalone Chunk program.

nodes.label: Smelting processor
nodes.detail: Reads the child tag after namespace 3 has been removed.

nodes.label: Market processor
nodes.detail: Reads the child tag after namespace 4 has been removed.

nodes.label: Unified PDA domain
nodes.detail: Account ownership and PDA derivation performed by routed child logic use the incoming Game program ID, not the standalone child ID.

nodes.label: Current client aliases
nodes.detail: backpack, market, and smelting currently resolve to the Game executable. Equal configured IDs are routing aliases, not proof of independent deployments.

nodes.label: Current Chunk route
nodes.detail: The current client addresses Chunk directly, so those calls use [childTag, childPayload...] and the standalone Chunk program ID rather than namespace 2.

evidence: The incoming Game program ID governs routed child PDA derivation
Current client config aliases Backpack, Market, and Smelting; Chunk remains standalone

diagrams.title: Identity and action authority are separated before gameplay writes.
diagrams.body: The current Core dispatcher accepts only the genesis initializer, while deployed upgrade authority remains separate evidence. Player tags include expiry-bearing sessions with caller-chosen duration, no revoke path, and non-consumed counter fields.

nodes.label: Equipment / Name / Invite

nodes.label: Backpack [8-11]
nodes.detail: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

diagrams.title: Guardian tags 0 through 5 manage realtime relay registration and liveness only.
diagrams.body: Tags 0-2 initialize the Registry and register Regions, tag 3 records an operator proof, tag 4 settles complete missed proof hours, and tag 5 lets the stored owner update the endpoint. Every higher tag is invalid.

nodes.label: Guardian [0-2]
nodes.detail: Initializes the Registry and registers genesis or adjacent 100x100-Chunk Regions.

nodes.label: Guardian [3-4]
nodes.detail: The operator submits proofs; any caller can settle missed one-hour intervals and reduce recorded stake.

nodes.label: Guardian [5]
nodes.detail: The stored Region owner updates host, port, and TLS; the operator has no endpoint write unless it is also the owner.

nodes.label: Registry / Region V1
nodes.detail: Stores relay registration, endpoint, role, proof, remaining-stake, penalty, and settlement fields only.

evidence: owner updates endpoint; operator submits proof
settlement is permissionless and reduces recorded stake

cpiAuthority.title: Audit game-facing cross-program writes by caller, callee tag, signer PDA, and public evidence.
cpiAuthority.body: These maps follow the current NiceChunk invoke and invoke_signed sites in Rust, so reviewers can see exactly which program is allowed to mutate another program's state and which PDA proves the write.

diagrams.title: Backpack has owner, session, and program-PDA mutation paths.
diagrams.body: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

nodes.detail: Moves an item between Backpack and PlayerEquipment through the Player-derived equipment transfer authority.

nodes.label: Smelting [2]
nodes.detail: Removes inputs matching the validated treasury RecipeTable, then appends Material outputs bound to that table PDA.

diagrams.title: Target-scoped adapters can execute a stored Civilization threshold result.
diagrams.body: Chunk and Smelting derive target-scoped adapter PDAs from a RuleBook. This prevents a generic target write, but the receipt may still rest on a 1 bps author-selected threshold, a finalizer-selected signature subset, and no enforced voting window.

nodes.label: Chunk [10/13]
nodes.detail: Applies resource-drop or surface-decoration Civilization receipts after validating the canonical Civilization program.

nodes.label: Smelting [4]
nodes.detail: Applies a Civilization recipe receipt before updating the exact identity-valid treasury RecipeTable target.

nodes.label: Chunk adapter authority
nodes.detail: Derived under the Chunk program from ["civilization-adapter", ruleBook], so a Smelting adapter cannot sign for Chunk targets.

nodes.label: Smelting adapter authority
nodes.detail: Derived under the Smelting program from the same seed family but a different program ID.

nodes.label: Civilization [3]
nodes.detail: Requires executor signer, RuleBook, Tally, Receipt, System Program, and adapter-authority signer.

nodes.label: Rule target binding
nodes.detail: The RuleBook names the target program and target PDA, so adapter execution is not a generic governance backdoor.

nodes.label: ExecutionReceipt
nodes.detail: Records execution for the exact RuleBook after its stored subset-based threshold result passes and the adapter signs; it is not complete-vote proof.

nodes.label: Target rule state
nodes.detail: Chunk and Smelting then mutate only their target-scoped rule table paths after receipt validation.

evidence: Receipt state is public but does not prove tally completeness or a voting window

accountLifecycle.title: Follow PDA state from rent funding to migration, growth, closure, or durable settlement.
accountLifecycle.body: These maps explain how current contracts handle pre-funded PDAs, rent top-ups, realloc growth, legacy migration, and refund paths without turning transient accounts into invisible state.

diagrams.title: PDA birth paths diverge: some adopt pre-funded system accounts, while others require pristine targets.
diagrams.body: Selected Core, Player, Guardian, Chunk, and player-progress helpers explicitly top up, allocate, and assign a system-owned PDA that already holds lamports. Backpack, RecipeTable, Listing, Civilization, and Building creation paths shown here rely on create_account and do not provide that dust-adoption branch. Every path still needs the expected seed, owner, length, and rent evidence.

nodes.label: Payer / owner / session authority
nodes.detail: Funds rent and must satisfy the program-specific owner, session, treasury, or seller authority checks before a PDA is created.

nodes.label: find_program_address
nodes.detail: The program re-derives the expected PDA before any create, allocate, assign, or write step.

nodes.label: Rent minimum
nodes.detail: The target length is converted into rent-exempt lamports before funding or top-up.

nodes.label: Empty PDA
nodes.detail: Creates the PDA with system create_account and the program-derived signer seeds.

nodes.label: Explicitly supported pre-funded PDA
nodes.detail: Only helpers with an explicit branch top up the rent delta, then invoke allocate and assign for a system-owned zero-data PDA.
nodes.evidence: Core / Player / Guardian / Chunk / player-progress helpers

nodes.label: Create-account-only target
nodes.detail: Backpack, RecipeTable, Listing, Civilization, and Building main creation helpers call create_account without a transfer/allocate/assign fallback; a dusted address is not handled by those paths.

nodes.label: Program-owned PDA
nodes.detail: The final account is owned by the expected program and packed with the current magic, version, owner, and GlobalConfig fields.

nodes.label: Lifecycle audit proof
nodes.detail: A reviewer can compare seed family, owner, data length, magic bytes, bump, and updated slot to verify the account birth path.
nodes.evidence: RPC account owner + data length + decoder

evidence: Dust adoption is helper-specific, not universal
Only explicit branches transfer the rent delta before allocate and assign
Seed and bump are checked before ownership changes
Decoded account length is part of the proof

diagrams.title: Temporary accounts either refund rent on cancellation or stay as durable sold-state evidence.
diagrams.body: Not every terminal action means the same lifecycle result. Appearance closure, building upload cancellation, and market cancellation reclaim lamports; marketplace purchase keeps the sold listing as settlement evidence.

nodes.label: Player [9]
nodes.detail: Only the treasury authority can close a PlayerAppearance PDA and receive its lamports.

nodes.label: Building [5]
nodes.detail: Cancels an uploading revision, zeroes and closes program-owned shard accounts, and closes the manifest.

nodes.label: Market [1]
nodes.detail: Restores the escrowed Backpack slot, clears listing data, and refunds listing lamports to the seller.

nodes.label: Market [2]
nodes.detail: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

nodes.label: Treasury authority
nodes.detail: Appearance close requires the recipient to be the treasury authority signer.

nodes.label: Session authority
nodes.detail: Building upload cancellation returns manifest and shard lamports to the session authority account.

nodes.label: Seller
nodes.detail: Cancel refunds listing rent to the seller; purchase pays seller proceeds and leaves sold-state evidence.

nodes.label: Zeroed closed account
nodes.detail: Closed Appearance, canceled Building upload artifacts, and canceled Listings are zeroed and no longer durable semantic records.

nodes.label: Sold listing record
nodes.detail: A purchased listing remains as a program-owned settlement record with buyer, sold slot, and sold time fields.

nodes.label: Restored or delivered Backpack slot
nodes.detail: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

nodes.label: Terminal-state audit
nodes.detail: Reviewers should distinguish canceled-and-closed accounts from sold records that intentionally remain decodable.

evidence: Canceled marketplace listings are closed and zeroed
Purchased listings remain durable sold records
Building cancel refunds upload artifact rent

payloadTruth.title: Separate user-supplied bytes from facts recomputed from PDAs, hashes, recipes, and rule evidence.
payloadTruth.body: These maps show which payload fields are accepted as selectors or intent, and which item, building, recipe, identity, endpoint, and governance facts are re-derived from contract-owned evidence before state changes.

diagrams.title: Marketplace listings use 19 bytes of intent, then escrow exact Backpack slot bytes.
diagrams.body: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

nodes.label: Seller signer
nodes.detail: The seller must sign and match the Backpack owner or equipped PlayerProfile owner before the listing is accepted.

nodes.label: CreateListingArgs
nodes.detail: Only listing_id, currency, source_type, source_index, and price_base_units are parsed from the user payload.

nodes.label: Backpack / profile gate
nodes.detail: Market re-checks Backpack magic, v3 owner, capacity, item count, PDA seed, and optional PlayerProfile equipment identity.

nodes.label: Slot lookup
nodes.detail: The selected Backpack slot must be a block or item record with nonzero quantity before it can be escrowed; block volume may still be zero.

nodes.label: Backpack v3 slot
nodes.detail: The source slot supplies the actual material, item PDA, coordinates, metadata, durability, and volume used by the listing.

nodes.label: Listing source_slot
nodes.detail: ListingAccount stores the full source slot bytes, so later cancel or purchase does not re-trust a new payload.

nodes.label: Cancel or buy
nodes.detail: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

diagrams.title: Uploaded building bytes become state only after shard completeness, hash, NCM3 parsing, and fit checks pass.
diagrams.body: The Building program accepts an expected hash, declared length, revision, rotation, offsets, and bounded shard writes. Finalization reconstructs the shard payload and re-computes every building fact that matters before activating a manifest.

nodes.label: BeginBuildingArgs
nodes.detail: Foundation ID, revision, quarter turns, payload length, expected hash, and optional X/Z offsets declare the upload target.

nodes.label: WriteBuildingShardArgs
nodes.detail: Each write names foundation, revision, shard index, offset, and bytes; oversized write payloads are rejected before storage.

nodes.label: BuildingManifest
nodes.detail: The manifest stores payload length, expected hash, shard count, rotation, offsets, and upload bitmap.

nodes.label: BuildingShard PDAs
nodes.detail: Shard accounts are tied to GlobalConfig, foundation ID, revision, shard index, uploaded length, and expected per-shard length.

nodes.label: Payload hash
nodes.detail: Finalize gathers every uploaded shard and rejects the manifest if hash_payload_slices does not match expected_hash.

nodes.label: NCM3 parser
nodes.detail: The parser requires NCM3 version 1, dimensions from 1 to 256, and at most 4,096 commands before deriving footprint height and width.

nodes.label: BuildSite fit check
nodes.detail: The derived NCM3 footprint must fit the BuildSite and world height after rotation and offsets; user bytes never set active dimensions directly.

nodes.label: Active revision
nodes.detail: Only a finalized manifest and BuildSite revision update represent durable building state; canceled uploads close transient shard evidence.

diagrams.title: Smelting and Civilization expose selected tables and supplied evidence, with provenance limits.
diagrams.body: RecipeTable identity and fixed treasury authority are enforced, while the Civilization finalizer still supplies the signature subset and no voting window is enforced.

nodes.label: Smelting execution payload
nodes.detail: The owner supplies recipe_id, input indexes, fuel indexes, and optional multiplier; the payload does not create output identity by itself.

nodes.label: RuleBook payload
nodes.detail: PublishRuleBookArgs stores hash commitments, target program, target PDA, total active power, threshold, target status, and risk.

nodes.label: RecipeTable
nodes.detail: RecipeRecord defines IO and yield inside a treasury-initialized table whose identity, fixed authority, and output provenance are enforced.

nodes.label: RuleBook
nodes.detail: RuleBook is a public target-bound commitment with an author-selected threshold as low as 1 bps; it has no voting-expiry field.

nodes.label: Backpack input validation
nodes.detail: The program validates RecipeTable identity and authority, then matches owner-validated Backpack slots before removal.

nodes.label: Signature and tally checks
nodes.detail: Signatures bind side and settled power; finalization rejects duplicates and impossible sums only among accounts supplied by the finalizer, without a Clock-enforced window or completeness check.

nodes.label: Selected-table smelting output
nodes.detail: Output volume is calculated from the validated table and inputs before SmeltingAuthority appends Material slots backed by that table PDA.

nodes.label: ExecutionReceipt
nodes.detail: Execution requires the stored thresholdMet result and target adapter, but threshold may be 1 bps and the tally may omit available signatures with no enforced voting window.

valueSettlement.title: Trace real token and lamport movement separately from item custody, rent, and governance evidence.
valueSettlement.body: These maps show where SOL or NCK actually moves, where rent is only funding PDA storage, and where gameplay evidence changes state without becoming a payment rail.

diagrams.title: Retired construction item
diagrams.body: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

nodes.label: Active ListingAccount
nodes.detail: The listing PDA must be active, writable, program-owned, seller-bound, and derived from [listing, seller, listing_id].

nodes.label: Escrowed source_slot
nodes.detail: Payment settlement does not invent item data; it reads the stored Backpack slot snapshot from the listing.

nodes.label: purchase_listing router
nodes.detail: The account list length and payment path depend on whether the listing currency is SOL or NCK.

nodes.label: 1% fee calculation
nodes.detail: split_market_payment computes fee = price * 100 / 10,000 and seller_amount = price - fee with checked arithmetic.

nodes.label: SOL transfer path
nodes.detail: For SOL listings, the buyer signs system transfers to the seller and MARKET_TREASURY after the treasury address is pinned.

nodes.label: NCK transfer path
nodes.detail: For NCK listings, token accounts must match spl-token ownership, NCK_MINT, and buyer/seller/treasury owners before checked transfers run.

nodes.label: MarketAuthority delivery
nodes.detail: Historical construction-item records are ignored and compacted by Backpack v4; no active issuance, equipment, marketplace, or land-registration path uses them.

nodes.label: Sold listing record
nodes.detail: The listing is marked sold with buyer, slot, and timestamp instead of being closed, so settlement remains decodable.

diagrams.title: Rent movement funds PDA storage; only explicit close paths return lamports to an authorized recipient.
diagrams.body: Rent funding appears across many programs, but it is not protocol revenue. Reviewers should separate rent top-ups and realloc funding from terminal refunds and durable accounts intentionally kept for evidence.

nodes.label: Payer / owner / session authority
nodes.detail: Initial account creation and rent top-ups are funded by the instruction payer, owner, seller, session authority, or treasury authority depending on the program.

nodes.label: Rent minimum
nodes.detail: Programs call Rent::minimum_balance for the exact target length before create, top-up, allocate, assign, or realloc.

nodes.label: Create or explicitly supported top-up
nodes.detail: Empty targets use create_account. Only helper-specific Core, Player, Guardian, Chunk, and player-progress paths adopt a pre-funded system account with transfer, allocate, and assign; create-account-only paths do not.

nodes.label: Realloc growth
nodes.detail: ChunkBroken/FoundationChunk and the supported Player profile, equipment, and appearance upgrades top up rent before reallocating larger account layouts; Smelting, Guardian, and Building do not expose a comparable generic realloc-growth path.

nodes.label: Listing cancel refund
nodes.detail: Cancel restores the escrowed Backpack slot, zeroes listing data, and transfers listing lamports back to the seller.

nodes.label: Building upload cancel
nodes.detail: Canceling a building upload closes manifest and shard accounts to the session authority after BuildSite pending revision is cleared.

nodes.label: Appearance close
nodes.detail: PlayerAppearance close requires the configured treasury authority signer and returns lamports only to that same recipient.

nodes.label: Durable sold / proof records
nodes.detail: Sold listings, rule receipts, and long-lived evidence accounts remain decodable instead of being treated as refundable protocol funds.

diagrams.title: Region owners transfer 100,000 NCK to the treasury; missed proofs reduce the recorded service stake.
diagrams.body: Registry initialization pins the treasury-authority PDA, treasury NCK token, NCK mint, and stake policy. Registration debits the owner token account. Permissionless settlement applies 10,000 NCK per complete missed hour and removes a Region when its recorded stake reaches zero.

nodes.label: Any payer
nodes.detail: Any signer may fund the one deterministic uninitialized Registry; the supplied treasury token must belong to the derived treasury-authority PDA.

nodes.label: GuardianRegistry
nodes.detail: Pins GlobalConfig, NCK mint, treasury token, Region size, stake and slash amounts, counters, and genesis state.

nodes.label: Owner NCK token
nodes.detail: Registration validates the owner token account, NCK mint, owner signature, endpoint payload, operator public key, and adjacency rule.

nodes.label: Treasury-authority token
nodes.detail: The destination token account is pinned in GuardianRegistry and owned by the derived treasury authority.

nodes.label: Stake transfer_checked
nodes.detail: SPL Token transfer_checked moves GUARDIAN_STAKE_AMOUNT from the owner token account to the treasury token account.

nodes.label: GuardianRegion V1
nodes.detail: The Region becomes active after stake transfer and stores separate owner and operator roles.

nodes.label: Permissionless settlement
nodes.detail: Each complete missed proof hour reduces recorded stake; zero stake marks the Region removed and decrements the Registry active count.

nodes.label: Region owner
nodes.detail: Signs registration, funds the stake, and updates host, port, and TLS.

nodes.label: Region operator
nodes.detail: Signs liveness proofs only; the current program has no operator-rotation instruction.

evidence: no withdrawal, refund, owner-setter, or operator-rotation tag

diagrams.title: Inventory, selected-recipe, mining, and proposal records can change state without moving SOL or NCK.
diagrams.body: Several high-value gameplay actions mutate PDA evidence or item custody, but they are not payment rails. Auditors should look for explicit system transfers or SPL Token transfers before classifying a path as value settlement.

nodes.label: Owner or session signer
nodes.detail: Mining and Building use session checks, while smelting and equipment use owner or program-specific signers. Civilization publication, tally finalization, and receipt execution accept any writable signer once referenced-state checks pass.

nodes.label: Program signer PDA
nodes.detail: Chunk, Smelting, Market, Player, and Building perform specific CPI writes through explicit PDA signers. Civilization records a receipt and validates a target-program-derived adapter signer supplied by the caller, but does not invoke the target program itself.

nodes.label: Backpack slot mutation
nodes.detail: Mined resources, smelting outputs, equipment transfers, and market deliveries change slot records rather than paying token balances.

nodes.label: Selected-table outputs
nodes.detail: Smelting matches Backpack inputs against an identity-valid treasury RecipeTable and appends table-backed Material outputs through SmeltingAuthority. No SOL/NCK payment occurs.

nodes.label: Civilization power records
nodes.detail: Power snapshots, citizen power, signatures, tallies, and receipts store authority-settled power and a finalizer-supplied subset threshold result. They are not spendable NCK or proof of complete, windowed approval.

nodes.label: Building and chunk evidence
nodes.detail: BuildSite, BuildingManifest, BuildingShard, FoundationChunk, and ChunkBrokenState are public state proofs, not value escrows.

nodes.label: Value-path test
nodes.detail: Classify a branch as money movement only when it invokes system transfer, create-account rent funding, close/refund, or SPL Token transfer_checked.

authorityBoundary.title: Separate compile-time roots, human keys, scoped program signers, and limits the current code does not enforce.
authorityBoundary.body: This audit maps the authority checks present in the ten native NiceChunk program crates, including the unified namespace router. A compile-time key or one-time account is not, by itself, proof that an upgradeable deployment is immutable. None of the ten programs defines a custom msg!, sol_log, emit!, or event structure; audit evidence comes from account state, transaction history, CPIs, and transfers rather than an event stream.

diagrams.title: Sessions enforce identity, an action bit, and expiry; the stored action budget is not live.
diagrams.body: Player tag 4 requires both the owner wallet and temporary key to sign creation or refresh. Consumer programs read the session record, but current validators do not consume max_actions, increment action_count, or provide an owner-only revoke or close path.

nodes.label: Owner wallet
nodes.detail: Signs creation or refresh, funds the PDA, and is bound to the PlayerProfile and session seed family.

nodes.label: Session authority
nodes.detail: Co-signs tag 4 and later signs high-frequency actions against its owner-bound PlayerSession PDA.

nodes.label: Player [4]
nodes.detail: Accepts BREAK_BLOCK and PLACE_BLOCK mask bits, a future expires_at, and max_actions greater than zero; it does not cap how far in the future expiry may be.

nodes.label: PlayerSession
nodes.detail: Stores owner, temporary key, PlayerProfile, GlobalConfig, world, allowed_actions, expiry, max_actions, and action_count.

nodes.label: Player / Chunk / Backpack
nodes.detail: Their live session branches bind the temporary key to the stored profile or owner, reject expiry, and require the selected action bit before mutation.

nodes.label: Building player actions
nodes.detail: The shared Building validator passes action index 1 for every player action. That index is BREAK_BLOCK, while PLACE_BLOCK is index 2.

nodes.label: Identity + bit + expiry
nodes.detail: These are the effective on-chain session limits: account ownership and identity bindings, the requested action bit, and expires_at greater than the current time.

nodes.label: Action-count budget
nodes.detail: max_actions is written and action_count is reset to zero, but the audited validators neither compare the two fields nor increment action_count.

nodes.label: Revoke, close, duration cap
nodes.detail: Player exposes refresh with both signers, but no owner-only revoke, session close, or maximum-duration rule; expiry is the only automatic cutoff.

evidence: Tag 4 requires owner and session-authority signatures
Only BREAK_BLOCK and PLACE_BLOCK bits may be stored
max_actions and action_count do not bound live calls
Building requests action index 1, not PLACE_BLOCK index 2
No owner-only revoke, close, or maximum expiry duration exists

diagrams.title: Civilization records a verifiable receipt chain, but its timing, threshold floor, and caller-selected tally set are material limits.
diagrams.body: The fixed power authority publishes snapshots and citizen allocations. Public callers may publish a RuleBook, finalize from the signature accounts they supply, and execute a passed receipt; actual rule mutation is implemented only by target-scoped Chunk and Smelting adapter paths in the audited code.

nodes.label: Power authority
nodes.detail: The fixed CIVILIZATION_POWER_AUTHORITY alone signs PowerSnapshot publication and CitizenPower settlement.

nodes.label: PowerSnapshot
nodes.detail: Commits total active power, epoch bounds, and optional expires_at under a snapshot hash.

nodes.label: CitizenPower
nodes.detail: Binds one citizen to a snapshot, exact power value, and inherited optional expiry before that citizen can create a RuleSignature.

nodes.label: Public payer / executor
nodes.detail: Any writable signer may fund RuleBook publication, tally finalization, or receipt execution once the referenced state passes validation.

nodes.label: RuleBook
nodes.detail: The author selects hashes, target program and PDA, target status, risk level, and threshold_bps from 1 through 10,000 against a valid snapshot.

nodes.label: RuleSignature set
nodes.detail: Each voter signs once with settled CitizenPower for the RuleBook snapshot and records agree, reject, abstain, or challenge power.

nodes.label: RuleTally
nodes.detail: Finalization iterates only the signature accounts supplied by its caller, rejects duplicate signers and aggregate power above total, then tests yes against required power and no.

nodes.label: ExecutionReceipt
nodes.detail: After a threshold-met tally, any executor may fund a one-time receipt; governable targets additionally require the target-derived adapter signer. The receipt records executor and time and is not a generic arbitrary-program mutation primitive.

nodes.label: Chunk / Smelting adapters
nodes.detail: Chunk tags 10/13 and Smelting tag 4 bind exact target program, target PDA, patch hash, tally, and receipt, then sign Civilization tag 3 with a target-derived adapter PDA.

nodes.label: Voting window and events
nodes.detail: Snapshot expiry is checked when nonzero during publication and signing, but RuleBook has no voting deadline and finalization has no time check. Civilization emits no program log events, so PDA state is the audit trail.

evidence: PowerSnapshot and CitizenPower require fixed 9Xuo… authority
Any payer may publish, finalize, and execute after state validation
The finalizer supplies the signature subset; duplicates and total-power overflow are rejected
Threshold accepts 1–10,000 bps and requires yes ≥ ceil(total × bps / 10,000) and yes > no
Only Chunk and Smelting expose audited mutation adapters; no RuleBook deadline or event stream exists
